quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one part of the lane and never move from it.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other vehicles see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so other drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as needed based on the road and traffic conditions around you.

questions.question: On a wet road, you should avoid:

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.
All areas of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of the lane. This strip loses traction when wet. You can ride to the side of this strip and still stay in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center portion of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the right portion of the lane.
Be flexible and consider many different factors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be flexible and consider many different factors.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Position yourself where other riders can see you and where you have space around you on all sides.

questions.question: For a long motorcycle trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel tired.
Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
Plan to ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on long trips, dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than 6 hours per day and take breaks at least every 2 hours. Do not use stimulants, as they cause extreme tiredness when they wear off.

questions.question: If a passing vehicle's wind blast hits you, you will have the most room to recover if you are riding:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the middle of your lane gives you the most space on both sides if a wind blast affects your control.

questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
Brake the front tire too hard and do not brake the rear tire hard enough.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not brake the front tire hard enough and brake the rear tire too hard.

questions.question: Where should you place a load on a motorcycle?

options.text: As low as possible.
As high as possible.
Behind the rear axle.
On one side of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them or put them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads against a rear bar or frame, as this raises the center of gravity and throws off balance. Always distribute loads equally on both sides.

questions.question: When a motorcycle operator's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means:

options.text: The operator plans to turn left.
The operator is about to stop.
The operator plans to turn right.
The operator is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The operator plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Operators may use hand signals instead of turn signals to show turns or stops. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the operator plans to turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you want to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve around a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left grip, then press the right grip to straighten. To swerve right, press the right grip, then the left grip.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is generally:

options.text: Pairs.
A staggered formation.
A single-file line.
A pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?

options.text: One second
Two seconds
Three seconds
Four seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: You should maintain a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase this to at least three seconds when weather or road conditions are poor.

questions.question: How do you swerve correctly?

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip in the direction opposite of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward. Press the opposite handgrip to straighten out after you pass the hazard.

questions.question: Which instruction should you NOT give a passenger before they ride?

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a large space between themselves and you.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should mount after the engine starts, sit as far forward as possible without crowding you, and hold onto the handlebars or your waist. They should keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and moving parts.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to stop a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Get them involved in activities to slow their drinking and keep them busy while they sober up.
Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends involved in stopping your friend from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: Good ways to prevent drunk driving include arranging another ride, involving them in activities to slow drinking, keeping them from leaving, and asking friends for help. Waiting 15 minutes is not effective.

questions.question: When do you NOT need a larger space cushion between vehicles?

options.text: The pavement is slippery.
You cannot see through the vehicle ahead of you.
Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
Traffic is heavy.

questions.correctAnswerText: Weather and traffic conditions are perfect.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions are poor. This includes slippery pavement, limited visibility, or heavy traffic.

questions.question: What is the best way to ride a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.
Change your path as needed.
Use the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your path as needed.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of a curve before straightening your path.

questions.question: The oily strip in the center of a lane is usually safe for motorcyclists unless:

options.text: It is never safe for motorcyclists.
The road is wet.
It is sunny outside.
It is always safe in all weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually provides enough traction. On wet roads, it becomes slippery. The strip is narrow enough that you can often ride around it while staying in the center of the lane.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear wheel while braking on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and down shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are generally smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards and conditions.

questions.question: What formation is best for a group of riders going around a curve?

options.text: Pyramid
Staggered
Single-file
Compressed

questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Use a single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway. A staggered formation works best for riding close together while keeping safe distance on straight roads.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight during the day?

options.text: Do not use it.
Use the high beam.
Use the low beam.
Switch between high beam and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the high beam.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day to help other drivers see you. Use high beam whenever you are not riding behind or meeting other vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do with your headlight when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use your low beam.
Do not use your headlight.
Switch between high beam and low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beam will reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: When riding at night, which is something you should NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Make yourself visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use high beam (unless meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to see, and wear reflective clothing. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and maintain safe distance. Do not stay in only one part of your lane.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another rider on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Move to the right part of the lane so they can see you in their side mirror.
Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
Stay in the center of the lane so they can see you in their rearview mirror.
Weave in your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the left part of the lane to see better ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to see better and to be more visible to other drivers in the passing lane. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic before changing lanes.
